_readme: Platform registry for Obi embed. 'platforms' = trusted JWT issuers keyed by platform key; an entry keys the trusted-issuer verification config. 'integrations' maps an integration CLAIM VALUE to the live obi-*-test knowledge scopes from knowledge_scopes.json. Each platform's 'allowed_integrations' (gap CIP-A1) lists the integration CLAIM VALUES that platform is trusted to assert: a self-serving platform lists only its own (mews->[mews], toast->[toast], opera-cloud->[opera-cloud]); build_auth_context REJECTS (401) a verified token whose 'integration' is not in the issuing platform's list, so a trusted issuer can no longer claim another tenant's integration. datahub's allowed_integrations ([mews,toast,opera-cloud]) is the HUB's vend set and is an OWNER TRUST DECISION (decision-needed): confirm the Data Hub is trusted to vend exactly these product integrations. Validated at startup (backend/app/platform/config/platforms.py): every mapped scope must exist in knowledge_scopes.json; every allowed_integrations value must be a key of the integrations map; 'classified' is never mappable; obi-general-test is added by the loader and must NEVER be listed here by hand; lifetime_minutes within 1..1440; every alg on the allow-list (RS256, ES256); outside local, zero active platforms stops startup. datahub is the first active platform (issuer/jwks/domains are TODO placeholders until Phase 4.x); mews, toast and opera-cloud are present and inactive. Entries with active=false are skipped by the frame CSP and the frontend loader, STILL verify a token if one arrives (by_issuer), but are DENIED scoped access at build_auth_context (AUTH-1/CIP-A2: platform_for serves only active entries). Tag names follow knowledge_scopes.json and are renamed with it before production.
